title: Tangled Traits (Lack of Interface Segregation)
pattern: A single large trait or interface bundles operations used by completely different, independent client consumers, forcing implementers to write dummy methods or panic handlers for unused interface operations.
why_bad: If an admin client requires a change to `rebuild_search_index`, the trait definition itself must change. This modification forces a complete recompilation and revalidation of all implementing types (including `SimpleViewer`), even though their local behavior is completely unaffected.
detection: Traits where some implementing types leave method bodies empty, print warnings, or return `panic!` / errors signaling that the method is unsupported on this specific implementer.
counterexample: Unified cohesive interfaces where every method is fundamentally required to maintain the logical state contract (e.g., an `Iterator` where both `next` and `size_hint` serve a single cohesive consumer).
fix: Apply the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP). Split the monolithic trait into smaller, highly cohesive traits (`ReadableDocument`, `WritableDocument`, `IndexableDocument`) and compose them as needed.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Architecture* (2017), Chapter 10 ("Interface Segregation Principle"), pp. 84-86.
